articles.title: Red Sox's Ceddanne Rafaela Reacts to Controversial Non-Catch vs, Yankees in Video, IG Photo
articles.summary: Boston Red Sox outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela appeared to have made an impressive diving catch in the fifth inning against the New York Yankees on Sunday, but the umpiring crew ruled that it hit the ground.
articles.body:
Boston Red Sox outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela appeared to have made an impressive diving catch in the fifth inning against the New York Yankees on Sunday, but the umpiring crew ruled that it hit the ground.

Rafaela reacted to the ruling on social media after the game.

"I know when a ball drops and a ball doesn't drop," Rafaela told reporters after the game. "I know I made the catch."

The game was tied 0-0 before the play, and it would have been the first out of the inning. Instead, the Yankees scored five runs after it was ruled a no-catch, completely changing the course of the game.

"Everybody was surprised by that call," pitcher Ranger Suarez said. "That was a game-changing play."

New York went on to win the game 16-1, marking the Red Sox's largest loss of the season.

It's hard to say whether the play being called a no-catch completely changed the game, but it's easy for the Red Sox to think that it was the turning point in the massive loss.

"It's frustrating; we had a really good baseball game right there, a zero-zero game," interim manager Chad Tracy said. "Obviously that play leads to the second and third, and (Paul Goldschmidt) rolls one up the middle and (Heliot) Ramos caps it with the home run. All of a sudden it's a five-run inning."

Boston has now lost four of its last five, but the Red Sox are still sitting in third place in the AL East and are five games ahead in the wild-card race.

articles.title: Complete MLB Playoff Bracket Picture 2026, AL, NL Standings and Wild-Card Race
articles.summary: The MLB playoff picture continued to take shape on Sunday.
articles.body:
The MLB playoff picture continued to take shape on Sunday.

Below we'll take a look at the full divisional and Wild Card standings and take a look at the top remaining races.

There isn't a ton of drama remaining when it comes to playoff seeds.

While there may be some reshuffling of seeds, a number of teams already feel like locks. The Rays, Yankees and Red Sox are all extremely safe bets, while the White Sox would need a pretty major collapse to both blow the division and fail to earn a Wild Card bid.

But the AL West remains wide open, and so does the chase for the final Wild Card berth. None of those teams seem likely to truly challenge the AL East trio once it comes to October baseball, but it only takes one hot team to shake things up.

There's even less drama in the National League, where the Dodgers and Brewers have all but wrapped up their division and Atlanta's recent seven-game winning streak has kept their lead over the Phillies to five games.

The Cubs and Phillies are also comfortably atop the Wild Card standings, leaving the major remaining drama the battle between the Diamondbacks, Padres and perhaps the Marlins for the final Wild Card berth.

articles.title: Elly De La Cruz Injured, Latest Updates and Timeline to Return After Reds Star Exits vs. Cubs
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Reds are hoping for the best after their star player exited with an injury against the Chicago Cubs on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Reds are hoping for the best after their star player exited with an injury against the Chicago Cubs on Sunday.

The team announced that Elly De La Cruz left the game with left quad tightness, and Joey Votto said on the NBC broadcast that the shortstop was "not in perfect shape" as he came out.

De La Cruz had been putting together a strong game before exiting, going 2-for-4 with a run as the Reds led the Cubs.

After Cincinnati's 7-5 victory, manager Terry Francona revealed that De La Cruz may be able to play on Monday:

The 24-year-old has notched 21 home runs, 60 RBI and 24 stolen bases while slashing .269/.349/.476.

A quad injury is not unfamiliar territory for De La Cruz. He played much of the second half of the 2025 season with what the team referred to as a "partial tear" of his quadriceps.

"If you look at his year last year -- and I think a lot of people don't know this -- at the end of the year, like toward the end of July, he was dealing with a partial torn quad," president of baseball operations Nick Krall said in November. "... "To his credit, he played every day. He tried to grind through it. He tried to play through it."

The Reds and De La Cruz hope the injury on Sunday isn't a long-term ordeal, but it at least could be something he's dealt with in the past.

De La Cruz also dealt with a right hamstring strain earlier this season that forced him to spend 10 days on the injured list, but he's been able to stay healthy since then.

The injury comes as the Reds sit in fifth place in the NL Central and eight games back in the wild-card race at 64-72. With their playoff chances slim, the team likely won't rush De La Cruz back on the field as they look to avoid a significant injury to their star.

articles.title: 4 takeaways from Red Sox-Yankees: Cam Schlittler, Cody Bellinger, Roman Anthony and Heliot Ramos all make their mark
articles.summary: The Sox had a chance to close the gap on the Yankees this weekend. Instead, New York further solidified the AL East pecking order.
articles.body:
For the Red Sox, this weekend offered a tantalizing opportunity: Take three out of four in the Bronx against the Yankees, and Boston would secure the season tiebreaker and leap its rival in the standings. It would've been a fulfilling culmination of sorts for a club that was, just a few months ago, very down and incredibly out.

Instead, the Sox were outplayed and outclassed in a disappointing series loss that likely complicates their path to postseason glory. An ugly 16-1 drubbing on Sunday , in which infielder Andruw Monasterio had to throw the ninth inning, was the frustrating cherry on the bummer sundae in which the Yankees took three out of four.

For New York, it was a reassuring result, one that further solidified the current AL East pecking order.

The AL East-leading Rays swept the Padres this weekend , pushing their division lead to 4.5 games over New York. That leaves the Yankees atop the wild-card race, despite having the second-best record in the American League . They're now four games clear of Boston, which is five games safe of the next-closest club in the wild-card race.

Yes, there's still a month or so of games to play. But the playoff picture is coming into focus, with this weekend's result making a Yankees-Red Sox wild-card rematch a very, very likely outcome.

The Yankees still have the rotation advantage

Last postseason, Cam Schlittler elevated himself from nice story to world-beater with a masterful, eight-inning, 12-strikeout performance against the Red Sox in AL wild-card Game 3. Less than a year later, the Massachusetts kid has evolved into a co-front-runner for the AL Cy Young Award alongside Toronto's Dylan Cease. On Friday against his boyhood team, Schlittler further reinforced his awards case with six brilliant shutout innings in a nailbiting 1-0 Boston victory . It was a reminder that, in a rivalry overflowing with accomplished hurlers, Schlittler is top of the heap right now.

He also pushes New York's rotation past Boston's, at least on paper. As of right now, a three-game showdown between these teams would probably feature Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole for the Yankees against Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle for the Sox. Carlos Rodón, Will Warren and the currently injured Ryan Weathers are other options for New York. Boston could turn to Patrick Sandoval or exciting breakout rookie Jake Bennett.

Fried's injury situation makes him something of an X-factor for New York, with the southpaw having navigated elbow discomfort all season. He returned from his latest IL stint over the weekend, working 3 ⅔ innings on just 63 pitches Saturday as skipper Aaron Boone opted for caution. Whether Fried can get himself back to his best self before October will be one of the Yankees' bigger September storylines.

Meanwhile, Boston's rotation, the club's backbone all season, suddenly looks a bit shaky. Suarez was abysmal on Sunday. The 36-year-old Gray is having his next start skipped. A return for Garrett Crochet, who carved up the Yankees in wild-card Game 1 last year, is looking increasingly unlikely. If he throws in October, it'll be out of the 'pen. Tolle and Bennett, exciting they may be, are both rookies. The Yankees have a much more reliable group.

Playing in a big-league game for the first time since May 4, the young slugger laced a double 101.6 mph to right field to lead off Sunday's game. It was a loud reminder of why Anthony, who missed nearly four months due to a right wrist sprain, was supposed to be the centerpiece of Boston's offense.

Debuting just a few weeks after his 21st birthday, Anthony stormed onto the scene last June and set the big leagues ablaze, coming good on his status as the sport's top prospect. An oblique strain kept him sidelined for the playoffs — a large part of why Boston tumbled out against its rival in the wild-card round. But even that truncated showing was enough for the industry to believe. Anthony was added to Team USA for the World Baseball Classic and homered twice. He entered the year as a dark-horse MVP candidate.

Then the wrist started barking and didn't stop. He relocated to the club's Florida complex to better focus on his rehab. In his absence, the Sox revived their season. But while the team shined without him, Anthony is a special, special hitter who should upgrade Boston's lineup immediately.

Cody Bellinger's defense remains a game-changer

The Yankees' glazy-eyed left fielder hasn't quite got going at the plate since he came off the IL last week. That should come with time. But Bellinger is already making a massive impact with his glove and his arm. In the seventh inning of Friday's game, with the Yankees clinging to a 1-0 lead, Bellinger delivered a 99.7 mph howitzer of a throw to nab the speedy Ceddanne Rafaela at home on a would-be sac fly. It was an outcome-altering moment, one that reinforced just how valuable Bellinger's glove is for the Yankees.

While Bellinger was out, New York was primarily rolling with trade acquisition Heliot Ramos in left, rookie Spencer Jones in right and the solid-but-unspectacular Trent Grisham in center. Ramos struggled in Yankee Stadium's spacious left field, an arena in which the fleet-footed Bellinger has grown comfortable over the years. His return pushes Ramos to right in a platoon with Jones, at least until Aaron Judge finally returns from his IL stint.

Heliot Ramos has his first big moment as a Yankee

Ramos, acquired from San Francisco at the trade deadline, had a bumpy first few weeks in pinstripes. Entering Sunday's game, he'd yet to homer as a Yankee and was carrying an ugly 7-for-59 batting line. But facing Suarez with two men on in the fifth on Sunday, Ramos lofted a loopy curveball over the seats in right. It was easily his biggest moment yet as a Yankee.

Ramos could be a crucial character in a Sox-Yanks playoff series, even if Judge returns in the next few weeks. Boston's rotation is extremely lefty-heavy, with Gray the only right-hander. The same is true for the back of Boston's bullpen, led by southpaws Aroldis Chapman and Erik Miller. Ramos has been meaningfully better against wrong-handers this season and throughout his career.

There's also a chance that Judge comes back healthy enough to hit but not healthy enough to play the outfield every day. That would push the three-time MVP to DH and leave an open spot in the outfield. How the Yankees would then sort everything out among Ben Rice, lefty-crusher Paul Goldschmidt and rip-roaring trade addition Luis García Jr. remains to be seen. But it might leave a lane for Ramos in the grass, particularly against southpaws.
